label: Sailor ID
help: The project Sailor ID for this man (the ID from the Reidy / NPS Black sailors database used in the prize-list matching). This is the key that links the pension to everything else, so check it twice.

label: Prize ID(s)
help: Optional. Prize ID(s) from the Abstracts of Prize Accounts that this sailor is matched to, separated by semicolons.

label: Status
help: P while you are working on it, C when the file is fully entered, K once a second person has checked it (10% quality check).

label: Minutes
help: Inputting time in minutes. Counted automatically while this record is open and you are active; correct it if needed.

label: NARA file / box reference
help: Archival location of the file as requested (record group, series, box or file number), copied from the request slip.

label: Scan folder or file name
help: Where the images of this pension file are stored (Dropbox / Drive folder or PDF name).

label: # images
help: Total number of images or pages in the scanned file.

label: # surgeons certs
help: Number of Surgeons' Certificates in the file. In the Union Army project these were set aside and entered as a separate dataset; count them here even if you do not enter them.

label: Checker notes
help: Corrections and general comments, good and bad. In the old workflow these went on an index card for the original inputter to review.

label: Name (LAST, FIRST M (COMMENTS))
help: Soldier's name. Name rule ('LAST NAME, FIRST NAME MIDDLE NAME'). Name information is found throughout the documents. All variant spellings must be collected in order to aid the census collection.

label: Where found / alias of
help: Optional: e.g. ALIAS, NAME AT ENLISTMENT, NAME AFTER FREEDOM, SPELLING ON DEATH CERTIFICATE.

label: App / Cert
help: A for an application number, C for a certificate number. Navy files were indexed separately from Army files; record the number exactly as on the slip, including any letters.

label: Number
help: Application and Certificate numbers are used to request the soldier's pension at the National Archives and are found in the General Pension Index (T-288/T-289). When the soldier applied for a pension, he was given an application number. If the pension was actually granted, he was assigned a certificate number, used by him and the pension Bureau for the duration of his pension. When the soldier died, his widow, minor children, or dependent parents could continue his pension. When they applied, they were granted new application and certificate numbers. Input these numbers from the Archives' REQUEST FOR MILITARY RECORDS form. This form is pink and attached to the file.

label: Claimant
codes: S=Sailor; W=Widow; M=Minor / dependent child; P=Parent
help: Whose claim the number belongs to: the sailor, his widow, a minor child, or a parent. Widows, children and parents received their own application and certificate numbers.

label: File type (Inv/Wid/Pa/Mnr)
codes: I=Invalid — the sailor only; W=Widow; P=Dependent parent(s); M=Minor or dependent child
help: The pension file's final classification. If only the soldier applied for or received a pension, record the file type as "I" (invalid). If the soldier's widow continues the pension, or receives her own, record the file type as "W" (widow). "P" designates a pension received by dependent parents and "M" a pension received by a minor child or a dependent major child. This information is apparent from the request form that comes with the pension.

label: Birth date
help: Date of birth. Found on enlistment returns (as age), affidavits, family circulars, Bible records and death certificates. An approximate date can be inferred from age at a dated event (quality code 6). Add a row for each discrepant birth date or place.

label: Q
codes: 1=About; 2=Before; 3=After; 4=During the war; 5=Discrepancy; 6=Inferred; 7=Muster-in/out (company or ship); 8=Since discharge; 9=At present time; B=Best date when a discrepancy is present

label: Complexion

help: Soldier's complexion. Use two-digit appearance codes. Appearance information appears in the Military Service record and enlistment papers.

help: Indicates the reliability of soldier's given complexion.

label: Feet
help: Soldier's height. Note that feet and inches are recorded in separate fields; convert all fractions to decimals. Height information is extremely important to this study. The date of each height change is equally important. Height is usually found in Military Service enlistment papers and war department records. It can also be found in affidavits and depositions.

label: Inches
help: Soldier's height. Note that feet and inches are recorded in separate fields; convert all fractions to decimals. Height information is extremely important to this study. The date of each height change is equally important. Height is usually found in Military Service enlistment papers and war department records. It can also be found in affidavits and depositions.

label: Q
codes: 1=About; 2=Before; 3=After; 4=During the war; 5=Discrepancy; 6=Inferred; 7=Muster-in/out (company or ship); 8=Since discharge; 9=At present time; B=Best date when a discrepancy is present
help: Indicates the reliability of the soldier's height information. Only label a height as a discrepancy (5) if a soldier is reported to have two different heights on the same date.

label: Date measured
help: The date at which soldier's height was recorded. MM/DD/YYYY. Height is usually found in Military Service enlistment papers and war department records. It can also be found in affidavits and depositions.

label: Source
codes: C=Certificate (official death certificate); L=Letter; P=Pension drop card; M=Military / Navy record; O=Other (affidavit, deposition, envelope…)
help: Indicates the most complete source of information about soldier's death. Death certificates include the date and place of death, the cause and contributing cause, and the length of the illness. Other sources are less complete. Pensions granted after 1915 have a much better chance of containing death certificates. Separate multiple causes with slash marks (/). Specify 'Other' source in remarks ('Death: Source xxxx'). If no death date can be found, add a remark with latest document date ('Death: No Date Given Last Document Dated xx/xx/xxxx')

label: Death date
help: Date of soldier's death. MM/DD/YYYY. If no death date is found in the pension file, add a remark with latest document date ('Death: No Date Given Last Document Dated mm/dd/yyyy')

label: Cause of death
help: The cause of soldier's death. Death certificates and military records (if soldier died in service) often contain cause of death. Separate multiple causes with slash marks (/).

label: Began
help: The beginning date of the cause of soldier's death. MM/DD/YYYY. Death certificates often include beginning dates for soldier's cause of death and contributing cause of death.

label: Contributing cause
help: The contributing cause to soldier's death. Death certificates can often include a specifically-labelled contributing cause; only when it is clearly marked on such a document should causes be listed here. Separate multiple causes with slash marks (/).

label: Began
help: The beginning date of the contributing cause of soldier's death. MM/DD/YYYY. Death certificates often include beginning dates for soldier's cause of death and contributing cause of death.

label: Illness lasted: yrs
help: The length, in years, of the soldier's terminal illness. Death certificates often include length of death illness. Input length exactly as seen on the certificate.

label: mos
help: The length, in years, of the soldier's terminal illness. Death certificates often include length of death illness. Input length exactly as seen on the certificate.

label: days
help: The length, in days, of the soldier's terminal illness. Death certificates often include length of death illness. Input length exactly as seen on the certificate.

label: Place of burial
help: Cemetery or place of burial if stated. (The old manual put this in Remarks; it has its own field here.)

label: Image #
help: Image or page number in the scanned file where this was found (e.g. 0042, or 41–43). Lets a checker or a later AI pass go straight to the source.

label: Date of entry
help: The date of soldier's immigration to the United States. MM/DD/YYYY. Death certificates often include immigration information.

label: Quality code for Date of entry
Or # of years in country
help: Number of years that an immigrant soldier has lived in the United States. Death certificates often include immigration information.

On rare occasions, a parent's name is found in the Military Service Record, especially in the case of a minor recruit. help: Indicates for which parent this residence information applies. Parents' residences can be found on pension applications, affidavits, depositions, letters, and envelopes. codes: 1=About; 2=Before; 3=After; 4=During the war; 5=Discrepancy; 6=Inferred; 7=Muster-in/out (company or ship); 8=Since discharge; 9=At present time; B=Best date when a discrepancy is present

help: The earliest known date at which parents lived at this residence. MM/DD/YYYY. If you come across another document with the same residence with an earlier date, delete the date already input in this field and replace it with the new, earlier, date.

label: Remarks — label each one, separate with ;
help: Remarks for Screen 1. All information collected in a Remarks field must be labeled according to the entry field it relates to (i.e. 'DEATH: xxxx'). The information in each Remarks field is specific to the screen on which it appears.

label: Name (MARRIED LAST, FIRST (NEE MAIDEN))
help: Wife's name. Spouse names are input in the following format: MARRIED LAST NAME, FIRST NAME MIDDLE INITIAL (NEE MAIDEN NAME; COMMENTS). For example, Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis would be input as ONASSIS, JACQUELINE (NEE BOUVIER; JACKIE). Do not repeat the soldier's surname. The family circular is the best source of information about the soldier's wife or wives. Spouse information is also found in affidavits, depositions, pension application forms, marriage certificates, death certificates, and letters.

label: Born
help: The date of wife's birth. MM/DD/YYYY. The family circular is the best source of information about the soldier's wife or wives. Spouse information is also found in affidavits, depositions, pension application forms, marriage certificates, death certificates, and letters.

label: Died
help: The date of wife's death. MM/DD/YYYY. The family circular is the best source of information about the soldier's wife or wives. Spouse information is also found in affidavits, depositions, pension application forms, marriage certificates, death certificates, and letters.

label: Married
help: The date of soldier's marriage to wife. MM/DD/YYYY. Marriage certificates are the best source for marriage information. The next-best source is the family circular. Widow's pension applications will also include marriage information.

label: Marriage place
help: The place of soldier and wife's marriage. The marriage place includes such things as BRIDE'S HOME, METHODIST CHURCH, etc.

label: Q
codes: 1=About; 2=Before; 3=After; 4=During the war; 5=Discrepancy; 6=Inferred; 7=Muster-in/out (company or ship); 8=Since discharge; 9=At present time; B=Best date when a discrepancy is present

label: Officiator
help: The officiator of soldier and wife's marriage. The standard name rule applies; comments include the title or position of the officiator, such as Minister of the Gospel '(MG)', Reverend '(REV)', Priest '(PRIEST)', or Justice of the Peace '(JP)'. Marriage certificates are the best source for marriage information. The next-best source is the family circular. Widow's pension applications will also include marriage information.

label: Div/Sep
help: Indicates whether the soldier and wife were divorced or separated. Information about divorces and separations will be found in the family circular and affidavits. If a separation is followed by a divorce, record the divorce information here and the separation information in the Remarks field.

label: Date
help: Indicates the date of any divorce or separation between soldier and wife. MM/DD/YYYY. Information about divorces and separations will be found in the family circular and affidavits.

label: Religion
help: Soldier and spouse's religion. Religion information is usually found on marriage or baptismal records.

label: Q
codes: 1=About; 2=Before; 3=After; 4=During the war; 5=Discrepancy; 6=Inferred; 7=Muster-in/out (company or ship); 8=Since discharge; 9=At present time; B=Best date when a discrepancy is present
help: Indicates the reliability of information about the soldier and spouse's religion.

label: Best source
help: The most complete source of marriage data. This field is intended to collect information on the source of the marriage data and should be updated as you come across better sources. It is important that this field reflects the best and most complete source document.

label: Image #
help: Image or page number in the scanned file where this was found (e.g. 0042, or 41–43). Lets a checker or a later AI pass go straight to the source.

label: Name
help: Child's name. The standard name rule applies; do not repeat the soldier's surname, but do record married daughters' last names. The family circular is the best source of information about the soldier's children. The next best source for children is the widow's pension application. Comments may include STEP, ADOPTED, and FOSTER. Unnamed children should be input as '(CHILD)'. Unnamed deceased children should be input as '(DEAD CHILD)'.

label: M/F
help: Child's gender. If it is not explicitly listed in a document, gender should be selected based on child's name.

label: L/D
help: Indicates whether the child is alive or dead at the date of the latest document found. The family circular indicates whether the child is alive or dead at the time of the circular. If additional information is found later in the pension regarding whether the child is living or dead, such as a letter written by a child to the Pension Bureau, update the information to the latest date.

label: As of
help: Indicates the latest date at which child is known to be dead or alive. The family circular indicates whether the child is alive or dead at the time of the circular. If additional information is found later in the pension regarding whether the child is living or dead, such as a letter written by a child to the Pension Bureau, update the information to the latest date.

label: Born
help: The date of the child's birth. MM/DD/YYYY. The family circular is the best source of information about the soldier's children. The next best source for children is the widow's pension application. Widow's pensions may also include childrens' birth certificates.

label: Q
codes: 1=About; 2=Before; 3=After; 4=During the war; 5=Discrepancy; 6=Inferred; 7=Muster-in/out (company or ship); 8=Since discharge; 9=At present time; B=Best date when a discrepancy is present

label: Died
help: The date of the child's death. MM/DD/YYYY. The family circular is the best source of information about the soldier's children. The next best source for children is the widow's pension application.

label: Q
codes: 1=About; 2=Before; 3=After; 4=During the war; 5=Discrepancy; 6=Inferred; 7=Muster-in/out (company or ship); 8=Since discharge; 9=At present time; B=Best date when a discrepancy is present

label: Name
help: Sibling's name. The standard name rule applies; do not repeat the soldier's surname, but do include sisters' married names. Sibling information is found in affidavits, depositions, letters, Bible records, and census forms. Sibling information is also found if a sibling provides testimony in an affidavit or deposition. Record STEP, HALF, ADOPTED, etc. or any title in parentheses. If the name of the sibling is not recorded, but there is an indication that there were siblings, record this information in parentheses: '(BROTHER)' or '(SISTER)'.

label: Born
help: The date of sibling's birth. MM/DD/YYYY. Sibling information is found in affidavits, depositions, letters, Bible records, and census forms. Sibling information is also found if a sibling provides testimony in an affidavit or deposition. Birthdates can be inferred from the document's date and the age of the sibling at the time of the document.

label: Remarks
help: Remarks for Screen 2. All information collected in a Remarks field must be labeled according to the entry field it relates to (i.e. 'DEATH: xxxx'). The information in each Remarks field is specific to the screen on which it appears.

label: Street
help: The street address at which soldier lived at a given time. Residential information is found throughout the pension record on many different forms, including all documents the soldier submitted to the Pension Bureau. While collecting a pension record, you must constantly update residence information. The correct use of quality codes is crucial for making this information comprehensible.

label: From
help: The earliest known date at which soldier lived at this residence. MM/DD/YYYY. If you come across another document with the same residence with an earlier date, delete the date already input in this field and replace it with the new, earlier, date. Residential information is found throughout the pension record on many different forms, including all documents the soldier submitted to the Pension Bureau. While collecting a pension record, you must constantly update residence information. The correct use of quality codes is crucial for making this information comprehensible.

help: The latest known date at which soldier lived at this residence. MM/DD/YYYY. While collecting a pension record, you must constantly update residence information. The correct use of quality codes is crucial for making this information comprehensible.

label: Name
help: The name of any person with whom the soldier is living. It is assumed that the soldier lives with his parents until he marries and with his spouse until she dies; if the soldier is living with anyone else, record that information here. This information can be found in letters and affidavits.

label: Relationship
help: The relation between the soldier and the person with whom he is living. Examples include SISTER, FRIEND, LANDLADY, EMPLOYER, etc.

label: Date
help: The date at which soldier is living with someone. MM/DD/YYYY. This information can be found in letters and affidavits.

label: Occupation
help: Soldier's occupation. Occupational information is found in enlistment papers of the Military Service Record, in declarations for pension, and in testimonial papers of the pension record.

label: From
help: The earliest known date at which soldier was employed at this occupation. MM/DD/YYYY. If you come across another document with the same occupation with an earlier date, delete the date already input in this field and replace it with the new, earlier, date.

label: To
help: The latest known date at which soldier was employed at this occupation. MM/DD/YYYY. If you come across another document with the same occupation with a later date, delete the date already input in this field and replace it with the new, later, date.

A percentage rating of the soldier's ability to do labor at a given time. Convert fractions to percentages, i.e. 1/4 is 25%, 2/3 is 67%, 1/2 is 50% and 'wholly disabled' is 100%. Labor force participation information is found most frequently in affidavits. It is often a subjective opinion of neighbors, co-workers, employers, friends, or family about the amount of work the soldier could do.

label: W/D
codes: W=Share of work he can do; D=Extent of disability
help: Indicates whether the percentage refers to the amount of work the soldier can do (W) or the extent to which he is disabled (D).

label: Or description
help: A description of the soldier's ability to do labor at a given time, if labor force is not given as a percentage or fraction. Labor force participation information is found most frequently in affidavits. It is often a subjective opinion of neighbors, co-workers, employers, friends, or family about the amount of work the soldier could do.

label: At
help: The date at which this labor force information applies to the soldier. MM/DD/YYYY. The date can either be the date of the document from which information is found, or a date specified by an affidavit (i.e. 'Soldier was 100% disabled as of 1876'). If multiple dates are given, create a window of time by inputting each date in a separate field.

label: State of finances
help: Soldier's state of finances. A soldier's state of finances is found in affidavits, depositions, pension applications, and letters. It is usually represented by key descriptive words such as DESTITUTE, GREATLY IN NEEED, or DEPENDENT ON CHARITY OF OTHERS. This field should always be filled out, even if the response is UNKNOWN (with no date).

label: At
help: Soldier's state of finances. A soldier's state of finances is found in affidavits, depositions, pension applications, and letters. It is usually represented by key descriptive words such as DESTITUTE, GREATLY IN NEEED, or DEPENDENT ON CHARITY OF OTHERS. This field should always be filled out, even if the response is UNKNOWN (with no date).

label: Type
codes: I=Income; W=Wages; R=Real estate; P=Personal estate; F=Financial; D=Debts; N=Navy prize money / back pay (added for this project)

Affidavits and depositions sometimes contain economic data such as wages or income. Anything dated within a year of the soldier's death is considered his wealth/income unless specifically stated otherwise.

label: Source document

Affidavits and depositions sometimes contain economic data such as wages or income. Anything dated within a year of the soldier's death is considered his wealth/income unless specifically stated otherwise.

label: Enlisted
help: The date of the soldier's enlistment. MM/DD/YYYY. Most soldiers have a specific muster-in card in the MSR that gives information about the soldier's enlistment. The date and place of enlistment can also be found in the pension record, both in oral testimony and War Department papers.

label: Q
codes: 1=About; 2=Before; 3=After; 4=During the war; 5=Discrepancy; 6=Inferred; 7=Muster-in/out (company or ship); 8=Since discharge; 9=At present time; B=Best date when a discrepancy is present

label: Age
help: Soldier's age at enlistment. The enlistment papers or the muster-in card from the MSR almost always gives age at enlistment. Do not infer age at enlistment from other sources.

label: Term: yrs
help: The number of years for which the soldier was enlisted. The standard periods of enlistment during the Civil War were 90 days, one year, or three years. This information can be found on the enlistment papers, either in the MSR or War Department papers. Record this information as it is found, i.e. do not convert 90 days to 3 months.

label: mos
help: The number of months for which the soldier was enlisted. The standard periods of enlistment during the Civil War were 90 days, one year, or three years. This information can be found on the enlistment papers, either in the MSR or War Department papers. Record this information as it is found, i.e. do not convert 90 days to 3 months.

label: days
help: The number of days for which the soldier was enlisted. The standard periods of enlistment during the Civil War were 90 days, one year, or three years. This information can be found on the enlistment papers, either in the MSR or War Department papers. Record this information as it is found, i.e. do not convert 90 days to 3 months.

label: Rating at enlistment
help: Rating (rank) given at enlistment, spelled out, e.g. LANDSMAN, BOY (FIRST CLASS), COAL HEAVER, FIRST CLASS BOY. "Contraband" was sometimes used as a rating for formerly enslaved men in 1861–62; record it as written.

label: Vessel / receiving ship
help: Vessel or receiving ship where he enlisted, as USS NAME (e.g. USS NORTH CAROLINA, USS PRINCETON).

label: Image #
help: Image or page number in the scanned file where this was found (e.g. 0042, or 41–43). Lets a checker or a later AI pass go straight to the source.

label: Vessel or duty
help: Specialized assignment or service performed by the soldier; examples include COMPANY COOK, MUSICIAN, TEAMSTER, or DETACHED SERVICE. Standard abbreviations for this variable are CO COOK, MUS, TMS, and DET SER. Information about duties is most often found in the MSR. For naval service, record the name of the ship the sailor served on, i.e. USS MERRIMACK, in the Duties field and the dates of his service on that ship in the From and To fields.

label: From
help: The earliest date at which soldier was assigned to his duty. MM/DD/YYYY. Information about duties is most often found in the MSR. If you come across another document with the same duty with an earlier date, delete the date already input in this field and replace it with the new, earlier, date.

label: To
help: The latest date at which soldier was assigned to his duty. MM/DD/YYYY. Information about duties is most often found in the MSR. If you come across another document with the same duty with a later date, delete the date already input in this field and replace it with the new, later, date.

label: New rating
help: Rating after a promotion, reduction or transfer, spelled out.

label: Date
help: Date of soldier's change of company. MM/DD/YYYY. A change in any of these fields is a change in the entire service; for example, if the soldier was promoted within the company, record the new rank and the company, regiment, and state, even if it is the same as the initial rank.

label: Description
help: Explanation of the change, e.g. PROMOTED, REDUCED, TRANSFERRED.

label: Discharged
help: The soldier's date of discharge. MM/DD/YYYY. This information can be found in the MSR (indicated on the Muster-Out rolls) and in the pension.

label: Hon/Dis
help: Indicates whether soldier was honorably or dishonorably discharged. Only honorably discharged soldiers were eligible for a pension. This information can be found in the MSR and in the pension.

label: Reason
codes: T=Expiration of term; D=Disability; R=Re-enlistment; O=Other
help: The reason for the soldier's discharge. This information can be found in the MSR and in the pension.

label: # days unfit
help: The number of days the soldier was unfit for duty before his discharge. Take this information directly from the Certificate of Disability for Discharge, found in the MSR and pension. Do not infer this information.

label: Cause
help: The reason why the soldier is unfit for duty. Take this information directly from the Certificate of Disability for Discharge, found in the MSR and pension. Do not infer this information.

label: Engagement
help: The place of battle fought by soldier. Battle information is found in all three Archival records. The MSR may give dates and battles for which the company was present. If a soldier was wounded in battle and treated in a hospital, battle information may be found in the CMR. In the pension file, battle information can be found in affidavits, depositions, War Department records, letters, and pension applications. Do not infer data for these fields. If you have different names for the same battle, e.g. ANTIETAM and SHARPSBURG, record the battle by the Union name (ANTIETAM). If you cannot determine if two names refer to the same battle, record both names.

label: Date
help: The date of the battle fought by soldier. MM/DD/YYYY. Battle information is found in all three Archival records. The MSR may give dates and battles for which the company was present. If a soldier was wounded in battle and treated in a hospital, battle information may be found in the CMR. In the pension file, battle information can be found in affidavits, depositions, War Department records, letters, and pension applications. Do not infer data for these fields.

label: Type
codes: F=Furlough / liberty; D=Desertion ("R" mark); W=AWOL / straggling; A=Arrest / confinement; M=Missing in action
help: Indicates the nature of the military action being described. The MSR is the main source for information about military action. However, the pension file is used to corroborate and often expands on information from the MSR because it determined a soldier's qualification for a pension.

label: From
help: The earliest date at which the military action applied, i.e. the beginning of a furlough or the date of desertion. MM/DD/YYYY. The MSR is the main source for information about military action. However, the pension file is used to corroborate and often expands on information from the MSR because it determined a soldier's qualification for a pension.

label: To
help: The latest date at which the military action applied, i.e. a return from furlough or desertion. MM/DD/YYYY. The MSR is the main source for information about military action. However, the pension file is used to corroborate and often expands on information from the MSR because it determined a soldier's qualification for a pension.

label: Place
help: The city, battle, camp, etc. where the military action occurred. The MSR is the main source for information about military action. However, the pension file is used to corroborate and often expands on information from the MSR because it determined a soldier's qualification for a pension.

label: Reason
help: The reason given for a soldier's arrest or desertion. The MSR is the main source for information about military action. However, the pension file is used to corroborate and often expands on information from the MSR because it determined a soldier's qualification for a pension.

label: Legal action / result
help: The action taken by the Army against the soldier, if arrested. Examples include CHARGES DROPPED, FINED, IN CONFINEMENT, CONFINED TO HARD LABOR, etc. The MSR is the main source for information about military action. However, the pension file is used to corroborate and often expands on information from the MSR because it determined a soldier's qualification for a pension.

label: Captured
help: The date at which soldier was captured as a prisoner of war. MM/DD/YYYY. Prisoner of war information is most often found on the POW form in the MSR; input information exactly as it appears on that slip. Information may also be found on War Department records in the pension file. Do not infer information.

label: At
help: The place at which soldier was captured as a prisoner of war. Prisoner of war information is most often found on the POW form in the MSR; input information exactly as it appears on that slip. Information may also be found on War Department records in the pension file. Do not infer information.

label: St
help: The state in which soldier was captured as a prisoner of war. Use two-digit state codes. Prisoner of war information is most often found on the POW form in the MSR; input information exactly as it appears on that slip. Information may also be found on War Department records in the pension file. Do not infer information.

label: Confined
help: The date at which soldier was confined as a prisoner of war. MM/DD/YYYY. Prisoner of war information is most often found on the POW form in the MSR; input information exactly as it appears on that slip. Information may also be found on War Department records in the pension file. Do not infer information.

label: At
help: The place at which soldier was confined as a prisoner of war. Prisoner of war information is most often found on the POW form in the MSR; input information exactly as it appears on that slip. Information may also be found on War Department records in the pension file. Do not infer information.

label: St
help: The state in which soldier was confined as a prisoner of war. Use two-digit state codes. Prisoner of war information is most often found on the POW form in the MSR; input information exactly as it appears on that slip. Information may also be found on War Department records in the pension file. Do not infer information.

label: Paroled
help: The date at which soldier was paroled as a prisoner of war. MM/DD/YYYY. Prisoner of war information is most often found on the POW form in the MSR; input information exactly as it appears on that slip. Information may also be found on War Department records in the pension file. Do not infer information.

label: At
help: The place at which soldier was paroled as a prisoner of war. Prisoner of war information is most often found on the POW form in the MSR; input information exactly as it appears on that slip. Information may also be found on War Department records in the pension file. Do not infer information.

label: St
help: The state in which soldier was paroled as a prisoner of war. Use two-digit state codes. Prisoner of war information is most often found on the POW form in the MSR; input information exactly as it appears on that slip. Information may also be found on War Department records in the pension file. Do not infer information.

label: Results
help: Description of results regarding the soldier's status as a prisoner of war, including transfers to other prisons, information about death, escape, furlough, etc. Prisoner of war information is most often found on the POW form in the MSR; input information exactly as it appears on that slip. Information may also be found on War Department records in the pension file. Do not infer information.

label: Service
help: Any non-Navy or earlier service mentioned in the file, e.g. 55 MA INF CO B, MERCHANT SEAMAN, USCT. One row per service.

label: Years
help: The number of years given for length of pensionable service. The length of pensionable service is found only on the pension ruling form in the pension file after 1907. Record this information exactly as it appears on the pension ruling form; do not infer or convert days to months.

label: Months
help: The number of months given for length of pensionable service. The length of pensionable service is found only on the pension ruling form in the pension file after 1907. Record this information exactly as it appears on the pension ruling form; do not infer or convert days to months.

label: Days
help: The number of days given for length of pensionable service. The length of pensionable service is found only on the pension ruling form in the pension file after 1907. Record this information exactly as it appears on the pension ruling form; do not infer or convert days to months.

label: Remarks
help: Remarks for Screen 5. All information collected in a Remarks field must be labeled according to the entry field it relates to (i.e. 'DEATH: xxxx'). The information in each Remarks field is specific to the screen on which it appears.

label: I/W
help: Indicates whether the problem is an illness (I) or a wound (W)

label: Description
help: Illness or wound with all descriptors, e.g. ACUTE DIARRHEA, CHRONIC RHEUMATISM, GSW L LEG, HERNIA, FRACTURE R ARM.

label: Severity
help: ACUTE, CHRONIC, FATAL, SEVERE, SLIGHT, FLESH.

label: Quality code for Date received / contracted
Hospital or ship
help: e.g. NAVAL HOSPITAL NORFOLK, HOSPITAL SHIP RED ROVER, IN QUARTERS (sick bay).

label: Result of treatment
help: RETURNED TO DUTY, DISCHARGED, TRANSFERRED, DIED, etc.

label: Image #
help: Image or page number in the scanned file where this was found (e.g. 0042, or 41–43). Lets a checker or a later AI pass go straight to the source.

label: Claimant
codes: S=Sailor; W=Widow; M=Minor / dependent child; P=Parent
help: Who filed: the sailor, widow, minor child (via guardian) or parent. The old screen assumed the soldier; Navy files often hold the widow's and children's claims too.

label: Type
codes: N=New (original); L=Increase — change in law; D=Increase — disability; R=Re-rating; I=Re-issue; A=Additional
help: Indicates the type of pension the soldier is applying for. Until the soldier was awarded a pension, all applications are considered 'New' (N), also referred to as 'Original' on the claim form. If the application is for an increase in disabilities (more disabilities or the same problems becoming more debilitating), input as an increase Disability. If the application is submitted due to a change in the pension law itself (which allowed more money for the same disability), input the application as increase Law. The only time you select 'Re-rating' 're-Issue,' or 'Additional' is if that specific word is written at the top of the claim form.

label: Application date
help: The date of the soldier's application. MM/DD/YYYY. The application date is found at the top of the Application/Declaration for Pension. That date is repeated at the bottom of the claim form. This field should never be left blank. If there are multiple dates to choose from, use the earliest chronological date.

label: Age
help: Age of soldier at time of pension application. This information can be found either on the pension application or the claim form. Do not infer age from any other sources.

label: Law
help: The law under which the pension was granted. Use this field when the law is described by name ('GENERAL LAW') or for any amendment dates.

label: or Law date
help: The law date under which the pension was granted. MM/DD/YYYY. If there are two law dates given, record both: the 'major' law (June 27, 1890, February 6, 1907, etc.) goes in this field and the amended law goes in the Law field.

label: Quality code for or Law date
Attorney
help: The attorney hired by the soldier to help them apply for a pension. Follows the standard name rule, with the following additions: in the case of attorney partnerships, the first name given follows the standard name rule and the rest of the information is recorded in parentheses at the end. For example, input Foxworthy and Co. as FOXWORTHY, (AND CO) and input 'John Smith and George Wesson as SMITH, JOHN (AND WESSON, GEORGE). Attorneys' names appear on both the application and claim forms.

label: Disability claimed / allowed
help: A disease, wound, or result for which the soldier was seeking a pension. Claims are listed in the Pension Application and at the bottom of the claim form.

label: Claimed
help: Indicates whether or not the soldier claimed this particular disability. Disabilities officially claimed by the soldier are listed at the bottom of the claim form as well as on the left-hand side of the middle column.

label: Allowed
help: Indicates whether or not the Pension Board approved this particular disability. Disabilities approved by the Board are listed near the top of the claim form, alongside the ruling amount, as well as on the right-hand side of the middle column. Please note that, in an application for an increased disability, the Board can approve the existence of disabilities without ruling in favor of an increase.

label: Ruling $ / month
help: The monthly dollar amount of the ruling given to the soldier. Convert all fractions to decimals. The Pension Board's ruling appears on the claim form, along with the pension commencement date, which usually corresponds to the Application Date.

label: Inc/Dec/Rej
help: Indicates whether the given ruling is an increase from the previous ruling, a decrease from the previous ruling, or a rejection. If the pension type is New, leave this field blank.

label: Ruling from
help: The commencement date of the ruling. MM/DD/YYYY. The Pension Board's ruling appears on the claim form, along with the pension commencement date, which usually corresponds to the Application Date.

label: To
help: The ending date of the ruling. MM/DD/YYYY. An ending date is given on the claim form in rare instances, particularly if the pensioned cause is expected to improve or the soldier dies during the application process.

label: Arrears from
help: Indicates the commencement date for arrears. MM/DD/YYYY. Arrears are granted to award a pension from the beginning of the wound/disease or to rectify a ruling deemed to be in error. Because the Pension Board granted arrears for a specified amount of time, arrears have both a commencement and an ending date.

label: Arrears to
help: Indicates the ending date for arrears. MM/DD/YYYY. Arrears are granted to award a pension from the beginning of the wound/disease or to rectify a ruling deemed to be in error. Because the Pension Board granted arrears for a specified amount of time, arrears have both a commencement and an ending date.

label: Writes (Y/N)
help: Indicates whether or not the soldier writes. Y/N. There is often a statement on the bottom of the claim form indicating whether the claimant writes (Claimant does _____ write'). If there is a statement to the effect that the claimant signs by mark, record N in this field. If it is ambiguous, leave this field blank.

label: Reason (rejection / decrease)
help: An explanation for a ruling in the case of a rejection or decrease. If the ruling is a rejection or a decrease, there will be an explanation for the change. The most common responses in this field are SOLDIER DROPPED or ADMITTED SUBJECT TO THE ELECTION OF THE CLAIMANT ALREADY ON ROLLS AT EQUAL OR HIGHER RATE UNDER OTHER LAW. If the reason is simply NO INCREASE, leave this field blank.

label: Image #
help: Image or page number in the scanned file where this was found (e.g. 0042, or 41–43). Lets a checker or a later AI pass go straight to the source.

label: Remarks
help: Anything about the pension history that has no field: special acts, suspensions, restorations, payments to guardians.

label: Deponent
codes: S=Sailor himself; N=Neighbor; F=Family member; C=Co-worker; E=Employer; M=Military / shipmate; X=Special examiner; D=Doctor; O=Other
help: Indicates the person giving testimony in the affidavit or deposition. We are not interested in the name of the person giving testimony, only their relationship to the soldier.

label: Signs
help: Did the deponent sign their name or make their mark? For family members (widow, children) this is a literacy measure for the household.

label: Date
help: The date the testimony was given. MM/DD/YYYY.

label: Type
help: Indicates a general idea of what the given testimony is about.

label: Type 2
help: Indicates a general idea of what the given testimony is about.

label: Pre/War/After
codes: P=Before the war; W=During the war; A=After the war
help: Indicates the general time period for the information in the affidavit.

label: Info date
help: The specific date, if given, of the information in the affidavit. MM/DD/YYYY.

label: Pertinent testimony (original wording)
help: A description the pertinent information from the testimony. Use as much of the original wording as possible.

label: Image #
help: Image or page number in the scanned file where this was found (e.g. 0042, or 41–43). Lets a checker or a later AI pass go straight to the source.

label: Former slave? (Y/N)
help: Record whether the soldier is a former slave. This information may be found in the MSR or pension record.

label: When freed
help: If you know when the slave was freed input it here.

label: At enlistment (Slave/Free)
help: If you know whether the soldier was a slave or a free man at the time of his enlistment, record that information here.

label: How freed
help: If stated: e.g. ESCAPED TO UNION LINES, MANUMITTED, EMANCIPATION, ENLISTMENT, PURCHASED FREEDOM.

label: Owner name
help: If there is information on the soldier's former owners, record it here. You can find information on the owner in the MSR of USCT soldiers and in their pension files. There is a More? to collect information on more than one owner.

label: $ paid for slave
help: Compensation for Service of Slave

label: Q
codes: 1=About; 2=Before; 3=After; 4=During the war; 5=Discrepancy; 6=Inferred; 7=Muster-in/out (company or ship); 8=Since discharge; 9=At present time; B=Best date when a discrepancy is present

label: Remarks
help: Remarks for Screen 9. All information collected in a Remarks field must be labeled according to the entry field it relates to (i.e. 'DEATH: xxxx'). The information in each Remarks field is specific to the screen on which it appears.

label: Age

label: Form date

help: Remarks for Screen 10. All information collected in a Remarks field must be labeled according to the entry field it relates to. The information in each Remarks field is specific to the screen on which it appears. If there is any information on the Veterans Administration form that you are not able to fit in the screen variables input it here.
